cues.text: How does a massive rocket lift itself off the ground when there is no air in space to push against?
That is the work of a liquid rocket engine.
See the twin tanks feeding fluid downward?
Liquid fuel and liquid oxygen are pumped from their storage tanks directly into the heart of the engine.
Now look at the glowing chamber at the center.
The two liquids mix and burn violently inside the combustion chamber, creating extremely hot, high-pressure gas.
See the gas squeeze through the narrow throat?
The high pressure gas rushes toward the narrowest part of the nozzle, speeding up dramatically as it is squeezed.
Now look at the wide nozzle on the right.
As the gas expands and exits the nozzle at high speed, it creates the massive thrust that pushes the rocket upward.
By burning propellants inside a sealed chamber and forcing the hot gas through a narrow nozzle,
a rocket engine turns chemical energy into the powerful thrust that carries us into space.
